question.problem:
The following table shows the fuel consumption rate, $F(t),$ of a generator (in liters per hour) over a period of $8$ hours.

| $t\,\text{(hours)}$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F\,\text{(liters/hour)}$ | $4$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ | $6$ |

Use the right Riemann sum for $F(t)$ over the interval $[0,8]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total amount of fuel used.

The total amount of fuel is 
{{field-1}} liters.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the step size $Δt,$ which is just the width of each rectangle. In this case, the endpoints of our interval are $a=0$ and $b=8,$ and there are $n=4$ rectangles, so the step size is

$$
Δt=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{8-0}{4}=2.
$$

The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{F(2)+F(4)+F(6)+F(8)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $F(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(t)$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ | $6$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(3+5+2+6)\cdot 2 \\  & =16\cdot 2 \\  & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total amount of fuel used over a period of $8$ hours. So, the total amount of fuel is $32$ liters.
